target: Error Recovery in Orchestrator — Test Case 9
executive_summary: The Harness Orchestrator implements a 6-layer defense-in-depth error recovery architecture. Errors at any layer are contained, logged, and do NOT crash the pipeline. The system employs both soft handling (empty results for nonexistent paths) and hard handling (try/except at agent and orchestrator levels). Verification rejection triggers up to 3 automated retries. After retry exhaustion, outputs are permanently rejected with structured rejection reports. The system always continues processing remaining agents.

LAYER_1.name: Agent-Level Soft Handling
LAYER_1.code: if os.path.exists(target_path): ... else: return empty result
LAYER_1.behavior: Nonexistent paths produce empty file lists (files_found=0, file_details=[]). No exception raised.
LAYER_1.catches: Nonexistent file paths, permission errors during os.walk (logged as warning)
LAYER_1.misses: Runtime errors, logic errors, unexpected exceptions in task execution

LAYER_2.name: Agent-Level Hard Exception Handling
LAYER_2.code: except Exception as e: self.status = 'FAILED'; self.error = str(e); raise RuntimeError(...)
LAYER_2.behavior: Catches ALL exceptions during agent execution. Sets status=FAILED, stores error message, then re-raises as RuntimeError.
LAYER_2.misses: Nothing — this is the last line of defense at agent level

LAYER_3.name: Pipeline-Level Exception Containment
LAYER_3.code:
try: agent.execute()
except Exception as e: outputs[agent.agent_id] = {'error': str(e), 'task_type': ...}
LAYER_3.behavior: Catches RuntimeError from Layer 2 (or any other exception). Stores error dict as output. LOGS error and CONTINUES to next agent. SYSTEM DOES NOT CRASH.

LAYER_4.name: Adversarial Verification Catch
LAYER_4.code: score = weighted_score / max(total_weight, 0.01); verdict = 'PASS' if score >= 0.7 else 'FAIL'
LAYER_4.behavior: Error outputs (missing fields, invalid types, inconsistent data) fail verification checks. 5 checks run: schema, isolation, consistency, completeness, security. Weighted score, threshold at 0.7.
LAYER_4.catches: Incomplete outputs, schema violations, missing required fields

LAYER_5.name: Automatic Retry Mechanism
LAYER_5.code: while retries_used < self.max_retries and verdict == 'FAIL': retries_used += 1; new_output = agent.execute(); re-verify
LAYER_5.behavior: Up to max_retries (3) automatic re-execution + re-verification attempts. Each retry calls agent.execute() again, then re-verifies. If any retry passes, output is accepted.
LAYER_5.catches: Transient failures, race conditions, temporary unavailability

LAYER_6.name: Clean Rejection & Isolation
LAYER_6.code: reject_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True); write rejection report JSON
LAYER_6.behavior: After ALL retries exhausted and verdict still FAIL: output is moved to outputs/agent-N/rejected/. Structured rejection report written with agent_id, filename, reason, timestamp. Pipeline result records rejected count.

execution_flow.step_1_fan_out: Both agents created with isolated environments
execution_flow.step_2_execute_agent_1: deep-read on valid path → completes with files found → status=COMPLETED
execution_flow.step_2_execute_agent_2: deep-read on invalid path → os.path.exists()=False → empty results → status=COMPLETED (soft handling — no exception)
execution_flow.step_2_execute_agent_2_alternative: IF path caused exception → status=FAILED → RuntimeError raised → caught by _execute_all() → error dict stored
execution_flow.step_3_verify_agent_2: Empty output (files_found=0) may PASS verification since schema is valid (0 is valid int, empty list is valid list)
execution_flow.step_4_retry: If verification FAIL: up to 3 retries, each re-executing and re-verifying

test_case_9_deep_dive.expected_result: PASS — at least 1 agent completes, system survives

retry_mechanism_details.exception_handling: If retry raises exception: verdict='FAIL', summary=str(e), loop continues
exit_conditions: exception in retry → verdict stays FAIL → continues to next retry or exhaustion
limitations: Retry does NOT call agent.determine() again — state may not be fully reset
If agent has systemic error, retries will all fail (waste of resources)

steps: 2. Write rejection report JSON with: agent_id, filename, reason, rejected_at

rejection_report_schema.reason: str — Why it was rejected (from verification summary)

findings: 3 retry mechanism for failed verifications (configurable, default max_retries=3)
Agent execution wrapped in nested try/except — inner (agent) sets status=FAILED, outer (orchestrator) stores error dict and continues
Nonexistent paths handled gracefully with empty results (soft handling at _execute_deep_read level)
System continues running remaining agents after one fails — no crash, no cascade
Rejection reports stored in outputs/agent-N/rejected/ as structured JSON with full metadata
6-layer defense-in-depth: soft handling → agent exception → pipeline containment → verification catch → retry → rejection
Adversarial verification uses weighted scoring (5 checks, threshold 0.7) to determine pass/fail
Fast 20ms mode has simpler error handling — quick_verify() returns PASS/FAIL without retries
Pipeline result tracks both agents_completed and agents_failed independently
Error recovery is TESTED explicitly via Test Case 9, which validates system survival

edge_cases_identified.behavior: Soft recovery — empty results, no exception. Agent status=COMPLETED with 0 files.
edge_cases_identified.implication: Test passes with 'agents_completed >= 1', but error recovery code path (exception → retry) is NOT exercised

edge_cases_identified.behavior: os.walk() raises PermissionError for individual files → caught by inner try/except → file skipped with 'error: Cannot read'
edge_cases_identified.implication: Partial result returned, no agent crash

edge_cases_identified.behavior: Layer 3 catches every time → error dict → verification fails → 3 retries all fail → permanent rejection
edge_cases_identified.implication: Wasted retry cycles but system survives

edge_cases_identified.behavior: Pipeline returns agents_completed=0, agents_failed=N. Test 9 assert fails (needs agents_completed > 0).
edge_cases_identified.implication: Pipeline itself does not crash even with 100% failure rate

error_recovery_rating.overall: Robust — crashes isolated, retries automatic, system survives
error_recovery_rating.soft_handling: Excellent — nonexistent paths, permission errors handled gracefully
error_recovery_rating.hard_handling: Excellent — comprehensive try/except at agent and pipeline levels
error_recovery_rating.retry_efficacy: Good — 3 retries, but no exponential backoff or progressive verification
error_recovery_rating.system_survival: Excellent — zero cascade failures, pipeline always completes
error_recovery_rating.edge_case_coverage: Good — most common failures handled, but some gaps in hard error triggering for Test 9
error_recovery_rating.fast_mode: Adequate — simplified quick_verify(), no retries, no rejection reporting

recommendations: Add exponential backoff between retries to avoid rapid re-execution of failing agents
Enhance Test 9 to trigger an actual exception (not just nonexistent path) to exercise the hard recovery path — consider injecting a mock that raises RuntimeError
Call agent.determine() during retry to fully reset agent state before re-execution
Add timeout per retry (currently uses the global timeout only)
Consider circuit-breaker pattern: after 3 consecutive failures on same agent type, skip further retries immediately
